correctness.rationale: The three leader types exhaust pair orbits of the weighted split graph. A grounded-Laplacian invariant-subspace decomposition gives exact inverse-trace formulas for each type (including direct boundary cases), and three rational difference identities reduce every peripheral-triad phase to polynomial sign comparisons. For p>=4, convexity with equal negative endpoint values excludes mixed optimality at small coupling; the controlling quadratic has a unique later root because it is negative at the earlier crossing and opens upward. p=2 and p=3 are resolved by exact specializations. Four symbolic identities, 420 exact independently inverted matrices, and 17 exact threshold checks corroborate the analytic argument without replacing it.

value.rationale: Core-periphery leadership placement is a natural H2-type stochastic network design problem. The infinite graph family with two homogeneous conductance classes is not an arbitrary enumeration: it captures a tunable core strength and admits only three structural leader pair types. The result supplies their complete analytic objectives, exact tie classification, and for a peripheral triad an explicit transition through all types with a coupling threshold of order p. Exact weight sensitivity and sharp reallocation are useful checks for approximate leader-placement algorithms.
